scope: OEM analysis/tool/test corrections; no new hardware validation and no OEM machine-code or configuration change

issues.title: F8.7 retry count and sticky mismatch were incorrectly described
issues.previous: v27 and final reports described at most ten copy/compare attempts and omitted the retained mismatch latch.
issues.root_cause: The comparison of the old counter follows the transfer; SETB C before SUBB A,#0A shifts the exit threshold. The latch is cleared only at function entry.
evidence: Persistent failure and first-failure-then-success both execute12 copies,4BC5=11,4BC4=1
issues.remaining: Analysis/model fixed. No firmware-policy correction is justified without the controller-window contract; see OEM-HW-01.

issues.title: USB setup wValue/wIndex were swapped in a historical fixture
issues.previous: v16 namedIRAM1C/1D as wValue and1A/1B as wIndex.
issues.root_cause: GET_MAX_LUN requires both fields zero, so symmetric final rejection tests concealed the swapped names.
evidence: GET_MAX_LUN wValue=1,wIndex=0 passesD970 then failsC702; wIndex=1 failsD970
issues.remaining: The original erroneous harness remains unchanged only in historical evidence.

issues.title: Zero-initialized projections were insufficient for stateful F2/E7 behavior
issues.previous: Clean-RAM enumerations did not exercise preservation of pre-existing state on inactive flag branches.
issues.root_cause: Several instructions only set a field when enabled; a zero fixture makes preserve and clear indistinguishable.
evidence: Earlier full initializer clears4588 and IRAMbits39/3A
issues.remaining: This is a coverage/model correction, not a demonstrated defect during stock boot.

issues.title: Return-only callee stubs did not prove native F8 register or interrupt effects
issues.previous: F8 dispatch traces with7616/77DA replaced byRET preservedR6 and interrupt state that real instructions change.
issues.root_cause: A branch-dispatch test was broader in interpretation than its stubbed execution contract.
evidence: Enabled realC4D3 chains finish with EA=1
71C4 consumesR7; the R6 difference is not itself a stock firmware bug
issues.remaining: Peripheral command/wait/control helpers remain explicitly stubbed; hardware DMA and concurrency are not modeled.

issues.title: Public byte-level tables could disclose the unit serial
issues.previous: Omitting a serial string from prose did not remove its individual bytes from the OEM CSV or raw hexadecimal output.
issues.root_cause: Redaction was applied to presentation rather than the canonical serialization boundary.
evidence: OEM056-077 is the serial payload region
issues.remaining: Private full atlas and original evidence intentionally retain source bytes; historicalv26 JSON must stay private.

issues.title: The33816 total mixed scenario counters, assertions and overlapping evidence
issues.previous: The aggregate was liable to be read as33816 independent functional tests or literal executed assertions.
issues.root_cause: Historical scripts count different units and repeat earlier bounded paths; hardware assumptions are injected by fixtures.
evidence: Unmodified expected values replay:33816 reported units pass
Dominant-method counts:28635 synthetic-memory native,2624 host-copy fixture,2316 peripheral/callee stubs,241 static/bookkeeping
issues.remaining: Neither count is a coverage percentage or hardware qualification. Native code is genuinely executed; the suite is not all host-language tautology.

issues.origin: Historical consolidation: already corrected in v29; independently revalidated here, not newly discovered
issues.title: E7.7 controls 5082 bits1/2, while bit3 is unconditional and later cleanup is independent
issues.previous: Earlier v27/v28 atlas text grouped bits1-3 under the E7.7 init option, which could imply all three were controlled by the flag or persisted together.
issues.root_cause: The old concise label omitted the distinct false-branch mask and independent cleanup consumers. Historical v29 already repaired this interpretation.
evidence: CPU D682-D699: flag set gives old | 0x0E; flag clear gives (old & 0xF9) | 0x08
Historical v29 build_atlas_v29.py and audit_v29.py contain the correct formula
issues.remaining: The physical meaning of these register bits and their scheduling on a live device remain unknown. This record preserves historical credit and does not claim a new factory firmware defect.

issues.title: Optional F8 retry-policy repair cannot yet be justified
issues.previous: The new analysis reveals retained failure state and redundant copies after a transient mismatch, but intended recovery behavior is unknown.
issues.root_cause: The7300/7500 windows and command/wait helpers lack a verified physical contract, including idempotence and completion timing.
issues.remaining: Need authorized instrumented hardware traces for immediate success, transient mismatch, persistent mismatch, controller response and reset; no flash-ready OEM patch is emitted.

additional_verified_refinements: All512 bytes and all32 flags have explicit categories; second half remainsUNKNOWN, not reserved.
JM gates the outer OEM loader;HD gatesE7/F3;BC gatesF2,timer,F8,FA/FB/FC.
Packed ASCII string type bytes are not validated by the loader; zero length skips conversion.
Timer arithmetic is32-bit modular; stock5 becomes1800 on the SCSI surface, or180seconds at100ms perunit; physical timing is not inferred.
70B6 arithmetic-command interpretation is context-specific;70C0-C3 is not a universally proven residue counter.
USB power reporting fields are descriptor claims, not measured current or power-switch control.
